scenario: Isolated copy of the 2026-11-04 pre-relay state: start records it as contract 0, a migrating upgrade selects the pool from the serial.log identity and clones the data disk, then rollback is refused without and completed with the discard confirmation

packages.original_state_package: created 2026-11-04 by an earlier package; its gateway endpoint records revision ac86fe9 from its last start on 2026-11-23

original.path: ~/.tama/incus-mac.backup-20261123 (the state moved aside on 2026-11-23; ~/.tama/incus-mac is a newer live state and was not used)
original.read_only: listed, fingerprinted (inode, size, mtime of all 25 files) and cloned; never started, written or opened by a service

isolation.state_dir: /tmp/macus-r57, an APFS clonefile copy (cp -c -Rp) of the original
isolation.incus_conf: /tmp/macus-r57-incus-conf, new and empty before the run; every incus and macus start command exported it
copy_adjustments: config.json and reboot-allowance.json held absolute paths into ~/.tama/incus-mac/appliance-cache, which is now the live state's directory; in the copy only the prefix was rewritten to /tmp/macus-r57/, so they name the copy's own cache as the original's named its own.

server/gateway.json (0600) was written with a free port (49320), as docs/development.md requires of acceptance states; the original's gateway used the default 8443, which the live default gateway holds.

steps.name: first_start_attempt_on_default_port
steps.note: Before gateway.json was written, the copy's server job crash-looped with eaddrinuse on 127.0.0.1:8443 and start waited at service activation for 10 minutes. The start was stopped and the copy's server job unloaded; no guest was booted. Isolation setup, not a product finding: the original state legitimately owned the default port at its own location.

checks.data_disk: restored from the backup's copy of 13:08:01Z (inode 122317874)

checks.refused_before_boot: This runtime's appliance guest was recorded with contract 0, below the contract 1 this Macus requires, so it was not booted. Run macus runtime upgrade to replace the appliance root; runtime data was kept.

notes: The storage identity written by rollback (source backup) is the upmaru/macus#20 review fix in becb6a6: the pre-relay state had no record, so without it the upgraded root's record would have stayed beside the restored data disk.

Post-upgrade writes are shown discarded by file identity: the restored data.raw is the clone taken before the new root's first boot, and the disk that received /root/r57-post and r57-post-vol is in safety backup 20261125T130940Z-149f171a. The guest-level discard was shown on hardware in the task 5.4 substitute run. A second upgrade to inspect it here was skipped because the host volume had 16 GiB free (99% used).
not_covered: Booting the restored pre-relay root, which only the earlier package can serve; the installed package correctly refuses it before boot.
Reading the old guest's Incus inventory before the upgrade, which the pre-relay bridge does not allow.
